newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU plans to clear Hydro Texaco/OK Petroleum scheme.
newsitem.headline: EU plans to clear Hydro Texaco/OK Petroleum scheme.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it intended to clear plans by Hydro Texaco Holdings A/S and OK Petroleum AB to create a so-called structural joint venture, Scanlube, for the production of lubricants.
The companies notified the European Union executive of their plan on December 1, 1995.
"The Commission intends to take a favourable position on the agreements...," it said in the EU's official journal.
However, the Commission said that before adopting a favourable position it invited third parties to comment on the deal within one month.
OK Petroleum, which is now called Preem, is a Swedish holding company which is active in exploring oil fields, refining crude oil in Sweden and marketing and selling petrol.
Hydro Texaco is a Danish holding company active in the retail and wholesale distribution of petrol, gas oils and lubricants and heavy fuel oils.

In November 1995, the two companies entered into several agreements, the Commission said. They asked the Commission for a a so called "negative clearance" or, as an alternative, an exemption from EU anti-trust rules.
"The aim of the joint venture is to acquire base oils, additives, packages and other supplies and to produce and package lubricants for sale to the shareholders," the Commission said.

In February last year, the Commission informed the companies that some clauses in the notified agreements "contained non-indispensable restrictions of competition" and urged them to formulate new proposals, which they did the following July.
"The clauses of the notified agreements that contained the restrictions of competition...have been withdrawn or modified by the parties in their proposal of 31 July 1996," the Commission said.
